record.prompt: Product wants a toggle flipped in the Nimbrel console to take effect in our running services within 5 seconds. Is that achievable, and what would it take?

record.final_answer:
Short answer: no, not on the current setup — 5 seconds sits below what Nimbrel polling can physically deliver. It's achievable, but only through streamed updates plus a code change on our side, and it carries a plan cost.

What the Nimbrel docs say (server SDK 4.x, read 2026-04-20):

  - default poll interval is 30s
  - the interval cannot be configured below 10s
  - push updates require stream: true on the client, and Team plan or above

Why tuning polling can't get there: 10s is a hard floor, and clients poll on independent, unsynchronised windows. A console flip lands at a random point inside each instance's cycle, so worst case is a full 10s, average ~5s. An SLO is judged on the tail, so 5s p95 or 5s max is unreachable even at the floor interval.

What it would take — three parts, and all three have to land:

1. Transport. stream: true on every service's SDK client, and the account moved to Team or above. That last bit is a commercial decision, not an engineering one — product should know the 5s ask has a plan upgrade attached. Streaming also means a long-lived connection per instance: check proxy/idle timeouts, reconnect behavior across deploys, and fan-out at their edge.

2. Read path in our code. The flag has to be evaluated per request or behind a short TTL cache. Anything captured once at startup — connection pools, worker concurrency, handlers registered behind a flag at init — will not change without a restart, no matter how fast the update arrives. In my experience this is usually the real blocker, and it's ours, not Nimbrel's.

3. Convergence skew. Between the console write and fleet-wide convergence there's a nonzero window where instances disagree. If the toggle changes behavior peers must agree on (routing, schema, auth), stamp a version and have readers refetch on mismatch rather than proceed on stale state.

Two things to nail down before anyone commits to a number: the clock starts at the console save, not at the SDK receiving it, so the console → flag-service write path is part of the budget; and which percentile the 5s applies to — 5s p99 across a large fleet is a materially harder problem than 5s p50.

Caveats on my confidence: I could not check any of this against our code, because /stand/ws is an empty repo — I don't know our SDK version, our plan tier, or where flags are read. The doc fact is from April and covers 4.x only; confirm we're on 4.x before relying on the 10s floor.

If the tier isn't Team or above, the honest options are: buy it, accept a 10s target instead (poll floor of 10s, p95 of ~10s), or build our own push channel from a console webhook into pub/sub — real work that duplicates what the SDK offers.

Suggested reply to product: yes at a cost — 5s is achievable with streaming and per-request evaluation, contingent on a plan upgrade and an audit of startup-time flag reads; polling cannot do it, 10s is the floor, so don't promise 5s on today's architecture.
